description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:1298-1303 (filter_to_ids) and 1392-1397 (apply_parameter_overrides) — Both methods are gated:

  #[cfg(feature = "oscal")]
  pub fn filter_to_ids(self, ids: &[String]) -> Result<Self, crate::oscal::parse::ParseError> { ... }

  #[cfg(feature = "oscal")]
  pub fn apply_parameter_overrides(
      &mut self,
      overrides: &[(String, String)],
  ) -> Result<(), crate::oscal::parse::ParseError> { ... }

Two distinct API-contract problems:

PROBLEM 1: FEATURE-LOCKING ON A NON-GATED TYPE.
LintRunner is the core type of the crate and is NOT feature-gated. Methods on it are. A caller writing:

  let runner = LintRunner::new(lints);
  runner.filter_to_ids(&want)?;

works in their initial code. When they later set default-features = false to drop OSCAL bloat, the method disappears. The compiler error is "no method named `filter_to_ids` found for struct `LintRunner` ... maybe enable feature `oscal`" — a feature-lock surprise the caller didn't sign up for.

The methods are filter/override operations that, in principle, do not need OSCAL — apply_parameter_overrides takes a &[(String, String)] of parameter overrides and applies them to lints. The OSCAL-feature-gating is convention, not a hard dependency: the methods themselves don't call serde_json.

PROBLEM 2: OSCAL-NAMED ERROR TYPE COUPLES LintRunner TO OSCAL MODULE.
Both methods return Result<_, crate::oscal::parse::ParseError>. ParseError is named for OSCAL (oscal/parse.rs:43 — variants are OSCAL-specific like ProfileImportUnresolved, ControlIdNotString, MetadataMissingProp). A caller invoking apply_parameter_overrides from non-OSCAL context (e.g., a CLI flag-based parameter override) gets back an OSCAL-named error type that has no semantic connection to their call site.

The result is that LintRunner's stable signature is forever coupled to the OSCAL module's error identity, and a caller reading LintRunner rustdoc must understand OSCAL to read the apply_parameter_overrides signature, even if they never use OSCAL.

REMEDIATION:

For PROBLEM 1: Move these methods out of cfg(feature=oscal). The underlying mechanics (Vec filter, parameter clone-and-set) are not OSCAL-specific. Keep the OSCAL-feature-gated convenience wrappers in the oscal/profile.rs module that translate from ResolvedProfile.

For PROBLEM 2: Introduce LintRunnerError as a feature-independent error type:

  #[non_exhaustive]
  pub enum LintRunnerError {
      UnknownLintId { id: String },
      UnknownParameter { lint_id: String, param_id: String },
      InvalidParameterValue { lint_id: String, param_id: String, source: ParameterError },
  }

Convert from LintRunnerError → ParseError at the OSCAL adapter boundary (in oscal/profile.rs) for callers who want OSCAL-style errors. LintRunner's public surface stays OSCAL-free.

Both fixes are pre-1.0 free. The Cargo feature-gating change is non-breaking-additive (broadens the feature set on which these methods are available). The error-type change is a breaking signature change but pre-1.0 permits it.

ALTERNATIVE: Document the cfg-feature-gating with a clear footgun warning in LintRunner's type-level rustdoc, and rename ParseError to something feature-neutral like RunnerOrOscalError. Cheaper but doesn't address the structural coupling.
title: LintRunner::filter_to_ids and apply_parameter_overrides are #[cfg(feature=oscal)] methods on the non-gated LintRunner type and return oscal::parse::ParseError; locks runner callers to oscal=on and exposes OSCAL-named error type at the runner level
